Class IntellijJava

java.lang.Object
uno.anahata.asi.agi.tool.ToolContext
uno.anahata.asi.agi.tool.AnahataToolkit
uno.anahata.asi.toolkit.java.Java
uno.anahata.asi.swing.toolkit.SwingJava
uno.anahata.asi.intellij.tools.java.IntellijJava
All Implemented Interfaces:
ContextProvider, PropertyChangeSource, Rebindable
public class IntellijJava extends SwingJava
An IntelliJ-aware extension of the core Java toolkit that can compile and execute dynamic scripts on the application JVM and against a specific open project's classpath.

This toolkit handles:

  • Automatic discovery of the full IntelliJ plugin classpath (combining IntelliJ platform libraries, bundled plugin dependencies, and runtime classes).
  • External javac compilation support when running on JetBrains Runtime (JBR) where in-memory JavaCompiler is omitted.
  • Project classpath resolution via OrderEnumerator for hot-reloading project bytecode.
  • Parent-first classloader delegation to preserve ThreadLocal context and singleton identities.

    • initialize

      public void initialize()
      Performs initial setup for a newly created toolkit instance.

      This method is called exactly once by the ToolManager after the toolkit has been instantiated and registered. It provides a clean hook for toolkits to perform one-time initialization logic that requires the tool environment to be fully configured, such as scanning for project instructions or registering default resources.

      Empty implementation as per architectural refinement. Initialization logic is moved to Java.postActivate() and Java.setDefaultClasspath(String).

      Registers IntelliJ-specific parent-first infrastructure classes and bootstraps the full IntelliJ plugin runtime classpath.

    • getSystemInstructions

      public List<String> getSystemInstructions() throws Exception
      Gets a list of system instruction strings provided by this context provider. These are typically prepended to the conversation as high-level guidance.

      Injects Swing-specific execution helpers into the system instructions, enabling the model to use runInEdt and runInEdtAndWait for safe UI interactions.

      Appends IntelliJ-specific guidance describing classpath architecture, JDK selection, and when to prefer compileAndExecuteInProject over the default compileAndExecute.

      public void populateMessage(RagMessage ragMessage) throws Exception

    • compile

      public Class<?> compile(String sourceCode, String className, String extraClassPath, String[] compilerOptions, JavaCompiler compiler) throws ClassNotFoundException, NoSuchMethodException, IllegalAccessException, InvocationTargetException
      Compiles Java source code into a Class object using the system's Java compiler.

      Compiles Java source code. If in-memory JavaCompiler is available, it delegates to the in-memory compiler in super.compile. If running on JRE/JBR where in-memory javac is omitted, it automatically delegates to compileWithExternalJavac(String, String, String, String[], Path).

      Overrides:
      compile in class Java
      Parameters:
      sourceCode - The Java source code to compile.
      className - The fully qualified name of the class.
      extraClassPath - Additional classpath entries to include.
      compilerOptions - Additional options for the Java compiler.
      Returns:
      The compiled Class object.
      Throws:
      ClassNotFoundException - if the class cannot be found after compilation.
      NoSuchMethodException - if a required method is missing.
      IllegalAccessException - if access to a member is denied.
      InvocationTargetException - if a method invocation fails.

    • compileAndExecuteInProject

      public Object compileAndExecuteInProject(String sourceCode, String projectPath, boolean includeProjectDependencies, boolean includeTestContext, String[] compilerOptions) throws Exception
      Compiles and executes a Java script against a specific open project's classpath.

      The project's compiled module outputs (and, optionally, its library dependencies and test scope) are resolved via OrderEnumerator and appended to the child-first class loader used by the core compileAndExecute.

      Parameters:
      sourceCode - the script source (a public class extending the core Swing tool base).
      projectPath - the absolute base path of the open project to run in.
      includeProjectDependencies - whether to include the project's library dependencies.
      includeTestContext - whether to include test outputs and test-scoped dependencies.
      compilerOptions - optional additional compiler options.
      Returns:
      the result of the execution.
      Throws:
      Exception - on resolution or execution failure.
